description: A clock generator with eight ratio channels: each channel runs at the master tempo multiplied by one number and divided by another, with an upright and an inverted gate on every one

params.text: Sets the internal tempo, 0 to 480 BPM
Attenuverts the clock CV before it is added to the tempo knob
Shifts every other beat of the master clock earlier or later, -99 to 99 per cent, which swings the whole set of channels together
Attenuverts the swing CV before it is added to the swing knob
Sets how much is added to the multiplier of any channel whose fill is on, 0 to 8
Attenuverts the fill CV before it is added to the fill knob
Sets how much of each cycle the upright gates are high, from a sliver to nearly all of it
Attenuverts the gate width CV before it is added to the width knob
Rotates the eight ratio settings round the eight channels, -1 to 1 for a whole turn in either direction
Attenuverts the rotate CV before it is added to the rotate knob
Sets how many times faster than the master tempo that channel runs, 0 to 128; at 0 the channel stops and its upright output stays low
Sets how many times slower than the master tempo that channel runs, 1 to 256
Adds the fill amount to that channel's multiplier while it is held
Starts the clock on each press and stops it on the next; the lamp beside it is lit while it runs
Returns every channel's phase to the start on each press and drops all the gates

inputs.text: Changes the tempo, added to the tempo knob at 10 BPM per volt through its attenuverter; the menu can read it as a volt per octave or as one volt per ten BPM instead
Changes the swing, added to the swing knob at ten per cent per volt through its attenuverter, the total clamped to -99 to 99 per cent
Changes the fill amount, added to the fill knob through its attenuverter and rounded to a whole number
Changes the gate width, scaled by a tenth and added to the width knob through its attenuverter
Rotates the ratio settings round the channels, scaled by a tenth and added to the rotate knob through its attenuverter
Sets the tempo from the time between two rises, in place of the tempo knob
A rise starts the clock, and the next stops it
A rise returns every channel's phase to the start and drops all the gates
Any voltage above 0.1V adds the fill amount to that channel's multiplier, which is what holding its button does

outputs.text: The master clock at the tempo shown on the display, a 10V gate whose width is set by the width control
The master clock inverted, 10V while the upright gate is low
That channel's clock, a 10V gate at the master tempo times its multiplier over its divisor; in phasor mode it carries a 0-10V ramp over the cycle instead
That channel's clock inverted, 10V while its upright gate is low; in phasor mode it carries the same ramp shifted by the width setting

notes: the clock does not run until it is started, by the ON/OFF button or a rise at the ON/OFF jack; the lamp beside the button says which state it is in
menu: Phasor Mode — replaces every gate with a 0-10V ramp over each cycle, the inverted output carrying the same ramp shifted by the gate width
Clock CV as V/oct — reads the clock CV as a volt per octave against the tempo knob, ignoring the attenuverter, so one volt doubles the tempo
Clock CV is 1V/10BPM — reads the clock CV as ten BPM per volt added to the tempo knob, ignoring the attenuverter
